title: Endpoint privacy modes and audit schemata for embeddings & rerank
creator: Priya Nair
description: Goal: Add endpoint-level privacy modes and a compact, standardized audit event schema for embedding and reranking requests so customers can enforce PII minimization, retention policies, and maintain compliant audit trails without leaking sensitive vectors or raw inputs. This ticket covers design, server-side controls, and a rollout plan for the embeddings/rerank endpoints (hosted and dedicated). The feature should: 1) expose opt-in privacy_mode per API key or route (modes: clear, minimal, redact, salted-hash); 2) stop logging raw input text/embeddings when mode != clear; 3) emit structured audit events with hashed identifiers and redaction flags; 4) support configurable retention windows per org; 5) provide admin flags for emergency full-audit (with elevated access and justification). This work must integrate with existing logging, telemetry, and the console retention UI.
acceptance_criteria: privacy_mode can be set at API-key, route, or organization level and respected by embeddings/rerank endpoints
When privacy_mode != clear, raw input text and raw vectors are never written to logs or debug stores

Audit events include standardized fields (event_type, ts, org_id_hmac, request_id, model, action, token_count, retention_ttl_days, redaction_applied) and exclude PII payloads unless privacy_mode=clear
Retention TTL honored by log ingestion pipeline and console retention selector; deleted events cannot be retrieved after TTL expiry
Admin emergency-audit requires separate justification flow; all uses of emergency-audit are an auditable event themselves
Unit and e2e tests validate modes across hosted and dedicated deployments and a simulated customer upgrade path
proposed_solution: Introduce a privacy_mode enum on API key metadata and per-route config: 'clear' (default), 'minimal', 'redact', 'salted-hash'
Server-side request pipeline will fork: sensitive fields will be removed/hashed before any logging/telemetry emission when mode != clear
Implement salted HMAC of org_id and user_id for audit events using customer-scoped salt in KMS; configurable rotation policy
Add a lightweight audit event schema (compact JSON) emitted to audit-topic (Kafka) with schema registry and Avro/Protobuf contract
Retention TTL metadata is written as part of each event and enforced by the ingestion/archival pipeline (retention-enforcer job)
Provide feature flags via console and infra toggles to enable emergency-audit with RBAC gating and an approval flow recorded in audit events
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): Implement server-side filtering and audit schema; run against internal traffic with privacy_mode defaulted to clear for all orgs. Duration: 3 weeks.
Phase 2 (opt-in beta): Expose privacy_mode to a small set of customers (beta flag); collect metrics on latency and log volumes; validate retention enforcement. Duration: 4 weeks.
Phase 3 (gradual): Make privacy_mode configurable in Console defaults; migrate telemetry and update docs. Provide migration script for orgs to set default policy. Duration: 2 weeks.
Phase 4 (hardening): Enforce privacy-mode logging constraints across Dedicated and Private builds; complete security review and compliance signoff. Duration: 2 weeks.
migration_notes: Existing logs that contain raw inputs will not be retroactively altered; consumers should use new retention filters to expire sensitive logs
Provide a one-time data-export tool for orgs that need to backfill redacted material before enabling stricter modes
Customers on Dedicated must run a small migration to configure local KMS salts for HMAC compatibility with hosted audit exports
tests_and_metrics: Unit tests for privacy_mode enforcement in request pipeline
E2E tests simulating minimal, redact, salted-hash modes across embeddings and rerank endpoints
Benchmark latency delta: target <= +10ms median for minimal/redact modes compared to clear
Telemetry: volume of logged payload bytes, # of audit events emitted, retention enforcer success rate
Security tests: attempt to retrieve redacted payloads from logs after TTL expiry (should fail)
